explanation:
[EFFECT] The effect is non-monotonic, with penalties at both extremes. Very low humidity (near 0 %) pulls contributions down to about −0.5; moderate humidity (roughly 20–60 %) keeps contributions near zero or slightly positive; and very high humidity (above about 80 %) causes contributions to plunge sharply, reaching as low as −0.8 near full saturation.
[IMPORTANCE] Sixth most important feature (importance 0.077); a moderate influence, primarily visible as a strong negative drag under very humid conditions.
[RECOMMENDATION] Staffing and bike-redistribution plans should be built primarily around the hour of the day — particularly the sharp morning (≈8 a.m.) and evening (≈5 p.m.) peaks — and adjusted for temperature, since warm mild days can roughly double predicted rentals compared with cold or very hot ones. All other factors, including weather and weekday type, provide useful fine-tuning but are secondary to getting the time-of-day and temperature conditions right.
